title: Sky Explorer
intro: Which stars in a photograph already have catalog measurements? Open the M46 field, mark its bright Gaia stars, and follow a point back to its catalog entry. You can also compare two views of the field or save your own annotated image.
dataset: The example uses M46.xisf, a color image with sky coordinates in its header. You can follow along with another plate-solved FITS or XISF image. For a first catalog search or a public survey, connect to the internet.
outcome: Identify a catalog star in a photograph, read its coordinates and brightness, measure an angular separation, and save an annotated image.
heroAlt: The M46 star field in Sky Explorer, with a dense concentration of stars near the center and a bright orange star toward the upper right.

groups.title: Open a photograph or a survey

steps.title: Enter Sky Explorer
steps.requires: Start Citizen Astronomy (CAst).
actions: On the mode launcher, find **Explore, Visualize & Process** and click **Sky Explorer** (1). From another workspace, you can also use **Mode → Sky Explorer**.
steps.check: The toolbar offers **Image** for a picture on your computer and **Survey** for a field downloaded from a public sky survey.
steps.alt: Sky Explorer card outlined among the exploration modes on the CAst launcher.

steps.title: Open the image picker
steps.requires: [Enter Sky Explorer](#launch). Have one image ready.
actions: Click **Image** (1) at the upper left. For this example, use the single file **M46.xisf**.
If you already have an image open, click **Replace** to start a new field. Choose [Comparison](#compare-prompt) if you want to keep the first image on screen.
steps.check: A file picker opens. A plate-solved image already contains the map between its pixels and coordinates on the sky.
steps.alt: Image button marked at the left end of the toolbar, beside Survey.

steps.title: Load the M46 photograph
steps.requires: The [image picker](#image) is open.
actions: Navigate to the folder containing **M46.xisf** and select that file. You can also type its full path in **File name** (1).
Click **Open** (2) and wait for the stars to appear in the image pane. If you are using your own exposure, select its filename instead.
steps.check: The field fills the right side of the workspace. For M46 you should see a crowded patch of stars near the middle. The **Explore** button is now available.
steps.alt: File name contains M46.xisf, with the field and Open button numbered.

steps.title: Start without a local image
steps.requires: [Enter Sky Explorer](#launch) with an empty workspace and an internet connection.
actions: Click **Survey** (1), next to **Image**. If a local image is already open, this button adds a survey as a comparison over that image.
steps.check: A survey picker opens. With an empty workspace, the downloaded sky field becomes your primary image.
steps.alt: Survey button outlined beside Image on the top toolbar.

steps.title: Choose a public sky survey
steps.requires: The [survey picker](#survey) is open.
actions: Click the survey list (1). Choose **DSS2 Blue** to follow the selection pictured, or choose another survey with coverage of your field.
Read the starting coordinates and field size below the list. Click **OK** (2). Wait for the center preview, then the sharper tiles.
steps.check: At the default coordinates the field is centered near the Trifid Nebula. After the tiles appear, you can run a catalog search on this field. Its objects and counts will differ from the M46 example.
steps.alt: Survey picker showing DSS2 Blue, the starting sky coordinates, and the OK button.

steps.title: Open the catalog settings
steps.requires: [Load M46](#open-file) or [open a survey field](#survey-select). To reproduce the count shown in this guide, use M46 and the entire image.
actions: Click **Settings** (1) in the main menu bar, then **Open Settings** (2).
steps.check: The settings window opens with tabs for the different workspaces. The next two steps set a bright-star limit and choose Gaia as the catalog for this example.
steps.alt: Settings menu open with Open Settings marked as the second target.

steps.title: Set a bright-star limit
steps.requires: [Open Settings](#open-settings).
actions: Select the **Sky Explorer** tab (1), then its **General** tab (2).
In **Gaia Max Mag** (3), enter **9.5**. Leave **Gaia Hard Cap** unchecked for this example.
steps.check: The field reads **9.5 mag**. Smaller Gaia magnitudes mean brighter stars, so this limit keeps the first set of labels manageable.
steps.alt: Settings showing the Sky Explorer and General tabs, with Gaia Max Mag set to 9.5.

links.label: Enable Gaia and save the settings

steps.title: Choose the Gaia catalog
steps.requires: Open **Settings → Open Settings → Sky Explorer → General**. For the pictured run, [set Gaia Max Mag to 9.5](#limits).
actions: Scroll to **Catalog Sources** (1). To reproduce this search, tick **Gaia DR3 Stars** and clear the other five sources. If you want to return to a previous setup, note its checked boxes first.
Click **Save** (2). When exploring another class later, return here to enable its matching source.
steps.check: The settings window closes. Gaia Data Release 3 is the available source for this run. You will next select which kind of object to draw.
steps.alt: Catalog Sources group with only Gaia DR3 Stars checked, and the Save button marked.

steps.title: Show the Advanced object list
steps.requires: An image or survey is loaded. For the example, use the [Gaia catalog settings](#catalogs).
actions: Find the mode button immediately right of **Explore** (1). Click it until its label reads **Advanced**. From the initial **Simple** list, one click is enough.
steps.check: The table now contains human-readable classes including **Star**. **Simple** lists common deep-sky classes. Continuing to cycle the same button opens **Scientific** for detailed classifications and **Catalog** for catalog names.
steps.alt: The Simple mode button marked beside Explore, before switching to Advanced.

steps.title: Clear the previous selection
steps.requires: The [Advanced object list](#mode) is visible.
actions: If **Unselect All** (1) is showing, click it once. If the button reads **Select All** and any rows are checked, click it to select every row and then click **Unselect All**.
If all rows are already empty, leave them empty and proceed to **Star**.
steps.check: The object checkboxes are empty and the button reads **Select All**.
steps.alt: Unselect All outlined immediately to the right of the Advanced mode button.

steps.title: Select stars as the search target
steps.requires: The [Advanced selection](#clear) is empty.
actions: Scroll within the object-type table to the **Stars** group. Under **Object Type**, tick **Star** (1).
Leave the other rows unchecked. The group heading can switch several types together.
steps.check: A check appears beside the **Star** row. Combined with the Gaia catalog setting, this asks for Gaia field stars.
steps.alt: Checked Star row outlined between Emission-Line Star and Young Stellar Object.

steps.title: Run the catalog search
steps.requires: A field is loaded and at least one compatible catalog source and object type are enabled. For the M46 count, use [Star](#star) with no region selected.
actions: Click **Explore** (1). Leave the field open while CAst checks its coordinates and looks up the selected sources.
The button reads **Terminate** while the search runs. Click it only if you want to stop the search.
steps.check: The results table fills and small markers appear on the image. With the saved M46 Gaia catalog and the 9.5 limit, 22 stars landed inside the image. A different field, limit, or selected region gives a different count.
steps.alt: Explore button outlined on the toolbar with the Advanced list active.

links.label: Check how many stars were found
Repeat the search in one region

groups.title: Inspect a result and the photograph

steps.title: Read the search summary
steps.requires: Run [Explore](#explore).
actions: Click **Work Log** (1) below the results table. Read the last entry for the field size and the number prepared for display.
In this run the cached search area contained **34** stars at G ≤ 9.5. The last line reports **22** in the rectangular M46 image.
steps.check: The log shows the source filename, selected object type, catalog and final count. A first online lookup can show download messages in place of the cached-catalog line.
steps.alt: Work Log tab outlined above the actual M46 messages reporting 34 cached stars and 22 plotted stars.

steps.title: Select a star in the results
steps.requires: A [completed search](#explore) has returned at least one star.
actions: In the results table below the object-type list, click once on a numeric name under **Stars** (1). Click the group header first if its rows are collapsed.
The example follows Gaia source **3029166186781118336**. Select any returned star in your own image.
steps.check: The selected row turns amber and the corresponding position is highlighted in the photograph.
steps.alt: Highlighted row for Gaia source 3029166186781118336 in the results table.

steps.title: Read the selected star’s measurements
steps.requires: [Select a result row](#select).
actions: Click **Inspector** (1), beside Work Log. Match **Name** to the selected row.
Read **RA** and **Dec** for its sky position, then **Magnitude** for its catalog brightness. Scroll down to see additional catalog measurements.
steps.check: The example star is at RA **115.096700°**, Dec **−15.264043°**, with Gaia magnitude **4.39**. The pixel position identifies where the catalog coordinates fall in this image.
steps.alt: Inspector tab and readout for the selected M46 Gaia source, including coordinates, pixel location, and magnitude.

steps.title: Center the image on your selection
steps.requires: A star is [selected in the results table](#select).
actions: Click **Center Object** (1) near the right end of the toolbar.
Look in the middle of the image pane for the highlighted catalog marker.
steps.check: The view pans to the selected position. Its Gaia name and catalog measurements stay attached to the same star.
steps.alt: Center Object button above the M46 image, with the selected bright star visible below.

steps.title: Open the display controls
steps.requires: [Load a local image](#open-file) to follow the M46 example, or [open a survey field](#survey-select).
actions: Click **Display** (1) on the top toolbar, just beyond the annotation tools.
steps.check: The menu contains separate controls for the primary image and a comparison layer when one is loaded.
steps.alt: Display control marked in the image toolbar.

steps.title: Choose an image stretch
steps.requires: Open the [Display menu](#display). A stretch maps the image’s brightness values to your screen.
actions: Under **Image**, open **Stretch** (1). Try **STF Bright** to bring up faint structure. Return to **STF** to reproduce the example view.
To return the image display controls to their defaults, click **Reset** (2). Click outside the menu to close it.
steps.check: The appearance of the field changes. The stars in the catalog table keep their original magnitudes and coordinates.
steps.alt: Image Stretch selector and Reset button outlined above the separate Comparison controls.

groups.title: Work in one region or compare images

steps.title: Search only a region of the image
steps.requires: A source is loaded and a [search target](#star) is selected.
actions: Click the dashed **ROI** rectangle (1), immediately after the text tool. ROI means region of interest.
Press and hold the left mouse button on the image, drag to the opposite corner of the area you want to search (2), then release. Click **Explore** to search that area.
steps.check: Inspect the results inside the dashed green rectangle. On a solved image its angular width and height appear near the top-left corner when that readout is enabled. When you want to search the full field again, click **ROI** to remove the rectangle and click **Explore**.
steps.alt: ROI tool and an example rectangle around a dense part of the M46 star field, with its angular width and height.

steps.title: Measure the separation between two positions
steps.requires: A [source image](#open-file) is visible. Clear an active ROI first if you want a clear view.
actions: Click the diagonal **Ruler** tool (1) in the drawing toolbar.
Press the left mouse button on the first position, drag to the second, then release (2). Read the label beside the line.
steps.check: The ruler links your two positions. On this solved image the label gives an angular separation in arcminutes, marked with a prime (′). Your result depends on the points you chose.
steps.alt: Ruler button and the drawn blue line with its angular separation outlined on the M46 image.

links.label: Save the image with the ruler

steps.title: Add a second image for comparison
steps.requires: [Open a primary image](#open-file). Have a second view of the same field ready. The example compares the M46 color frame with its red channel saved as a monochrome FITS file.
actions: Click **Image** again. In **Image already loaded**, click **Comparison** (1) to keep the original in the viewer.
Select your second file in the picker and click **Open**. For a pixel-by-pixel comparison, use two images registered to the same field.
steps.check: A vertical divider appears over the two images. **Replace** in the source prompt starts over with a different primary field.
steps.alt: Image already loaded prompt with Comparison outlined beside Replace.

steps.title: Move the divider across the same stars
steps.requires: A [comparison image](#compare-prompt) is visible.
actions: Place the pointer on the small white handle in the middle of the vertical divider (1). Hold the left mouse button and drag it horizontally.
In this example, drag right to reveal more of the original color field. Drag left to show more of the monochrome red-channel view. Compare the same bright star on both sides.
steps.check: The same stars stay in place while the color boundary moves. Switch between the two screenshots below the instructions to see both handle positions.
steps.alt: Divider handle marked near the left side with most of the M46 field shown in monochrome.

comparison.label: Divider at right
comparison.alt: The same M46 stars with the marked divider on the right and more of the original color photograph exposed.

steps.title: Choose the annotated image export
steps.requires: Open a local image and leave the [catalog markers](#explore) or [ruler](#ruler) you want to include on screen.
actions: Click **Export** (1) at the right end of the toolbar, then **Image…** (2).
If you are working with a survey and want that layer instead, choose **Survey…** when it is available.
steps.check: A save dialog opens for the annotated image. The exported image uses the original image resolution.
steps.alt: Export menu open with the Export button and Image action numbered; Survey and Animation also appear.

steps.title: Name the file and save it
steps.requires: Choose [Export → Image…](#export).
actions: Choose the destination folder in the file picker. Enter a new filename such as **M46-study.png** in **File name** (1).
Keep **PNG Files** selected and click **Save** (2). Open the saved PNG from that folder to inspect the markers at full resolution.
steps.check: The saved PNG contains the photographed field and its visible annotations. The M46 example exports at **2742 × 2460** pixels.
steps.alt: Save dialog showing M46-study.png, the PNG file type, and the marked Save button.
